title: The Organization of Behavior
core_idea: "Neurons that fire together wire together" — cell assemblies form via correlated activity.
why_it_matters: The first learning rule; Oja's PCA (domain 01) and all Hebbian methods descend from it.

title: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model
core_idea: A learnable threshold neuron with a convergence proof for linearly separable data.
why_it_matters: First artificial neural network trained by a rule; launched (and, with Minsky, froze) the field.

title: Perceptrons
core_idea: Proves single-layer perceptrons cannot compute XOR; (over-)read as killing neural networks.
why_it_matters: First AI winter trigger; its real lesson — depth or hidden layers are necessary — took 17 years to answer (backprop).

title: Learning Internal Representations by Error Propagation (PDP, vol. 1)
authors: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, Ronald Williams
link: MIT Press (chapter); companion: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, Nature 323 (1986)
core_idea: Multilayer networks trained end-to-end by backpropagated error signals.
why_it_matters: Reopened the field; every gradient-trained system since (all of them) uses this.

title: Generalization and Network Design Strategies
core_idea: "Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition" (LeCun, Bottou, Bengio, Haffner, Proc. IEEE) industrialized it as LeNet-5.
why_it_matters: The convolutional prior — the strongest demonstration that architecture = inductive bias (domain 01, F2); banks read checks with this in the 1990s.

title: Untersuchungen zu dynamischen neuronalen Netzen (vanishing gradients)
authors: Sepp Hochreiter (diploma thesis, advisor J. Schmidhuber)
core_idea: Gradients through deep/squashing activations decay or explode exponentially — the "fundamental deep learning problem."
why_it_matters: Named the obstacle that residuates every architecture decision for 25 years (LSTM, ReLU, residuals, normalization).

title: Long Short-Term Memory
core_idea: Gated memory cells let gradients persist across hundreds of timesteps.
why_it_matters: THE sequence model 1997–2017 (translation, speech); gates and state-carrying cells reincarnate as the transformer's residual stream with memory roles.

title: Q-Learning
core_idea: Learn action values by bootstrapping temporal-difference errors — no model of the world needed.
why_it_matters: The bridge to neuroscience: dopamine neurons compute exactly this signal (Schultz 1997, domain 04); foundation of all value-based RL.

title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Geoffrey Hinton
core_idea: GPU-trained deep CNN cuts ImageNet error nearly in half (16.4% vs 26.2%).
why_it_matters: The big bang of the modern era — proof that scale (data × compute × depth) wins; ignited the decade of deep learning.

title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases (word2vec)
core_idea: Skip-gram with negative sampling learns vector embeddings where directions carry meaning (king − man + woman ≈ queen).
why_it_matters: Meaning as geometry — the first widely-used demonstration that prediction-trained vectors encode semantics; the "embedding" concept every LLM uses internally.

title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
core_idea: Variational inference made amenable by reparameterization; encoder/decoder learn probabilistic latent representations.
why_it_matters: Founded deep generative modeling; the ELBO objective returns in diffusion theory and in "analysis-by-synthesis" brain models (domain 04).

title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
authors: Ilya Sutskever, Oriol Vinyals, Quoc Le
core_idea: Encode a sentence into a fixed vector, then decode it into another language.
why_it_matters: Established the encoder-decoder paradigm — and its fixed-vector bottleneck, which attention (next entry) was invented to remove.

title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
authors: Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, Yoshua Bengio
core_idea: Attention: the decoder dynamically looks back at all encoder states instead of one vector.
why_it_matters: Invented attention as a soft, differentiable lookup — the mechanism the transformer made foundational (domain 03).

title: Generative Adversarial Networks
core_idea: Generator and discriminator locked in adversarial minimax; sample generation without explicit likelihoods.
why_it_matters: Adversarial self-play as a learning signal — concept recycled in debate-based alignment and adversarial eval (domain 05); also the instability case study that made the field take training dynamics seriously.

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
core_idea: Per-parameter adaptive moments; robust default step sizes.
why_it_matters: The optimization workhorse (with AdamW variant) behind essentially all deep learning including LLM pretraining.

title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training
core_idea: Normalize layer inputs per minibatch to stabilize activation statistics.
why_it_matters: Made very deep training stable; its successor LayerNorm/RMSNorm is a fixed component of every transformer block.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun
core_idea: Learn residual functions with identity shortcuts → 100+ layer networks trainable.
why_it_matters: The residual stream is the transformer's backbone; loss-landscape geometry (domain 01, F7) explains WHY it works. Arguably the most reused architectural idea in history.

title: Human-Level Control Through Deep Reinforcement Learning
core_idea: Deep Q-network: CNN + Q-learning + experience replay + target networks learns Atari from raw pixels.
why_it_matters: First human-level learning from raw perception; experience replay explicitly borrowed from hippocampal replay (domain 04) — the neuro-AI transfer landmark.

title: Neural Turing Machines
authors: Alex Graves, Greg Wayne, Ivo Danihelka
core_idea: Differentiable external memory addressed by content and location.
why_it_matters: Opened the external-memory line (DNC 2016) — memory as an architectural component rather than emergent state; feeds directly into RAG and agent memory design (domain 05).

title: Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search (AlphaGo)
core_idea: Policy/value networks guided Monte-Carlo tree search; trained on human games then self-play.
why_it_matters: Search + learned evaluation beats pure scale; the template that returns in reasoning models (o1/R1 style test-time search, domain 03).

title: Mastering Chess and Shogi by Self-Play (AlphaZero) / [2020] MuZero
authors: David Silver, Julian Schrittwieser et al.
core_idea: AlphaZero: self-play alone reaches superhuman Go/chess/shogi. MuZero: learns a latent world model and plans in it — no rules given.
why_it_matters: MuZero is the proof-of-concept that LEARNED world models + planning scale — the thesis of modern world-model research (domain 05).

title: Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding
authors: Aaron van den Oord, Yazhe Li, Oriol Vinyals
core_idea: InfoNCE: learn representations by identifying the true future among negatives — maximizes mutual information.
why_it_matters: The single loss behind SimCLR/MoCo/CLIP and many RL representation methods; predictive coding's engineering counterpart (domain 04).

title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations (SimCLR)
authors: Ting Chen, Simon Kornblith, Mohammad Norouzi, Geoffrey Hinton
core_idea: Augment-crop-contrast with big batches and projection heads alone learns strong visual features.
why_it_matters: Showed the recipe, not the architecture, drives self-supervised vision; killed the label bottleneck for pretraining.

title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning (MoCo)
core_idea: Dictionary-as-queue with momentum encoder makes contrastive learning practical without huge batches.
why_it_matters: With SimCLR, established that contrastive pretraining transfers to detection/segmentation beyond supervised ImageNet pretraining — a capability transfer precedent for all foundation models.

title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision (CLIP)
core_idea: Contrastively align images and text captions at web scale → zero-shot classification by prompting.
why_it_matters: Multimodal grounding; zero-shot transfer as a paradigm; the backbone of image generators' text encoders and multimodal LLMs.

title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
core_idea: Generate by slowly destroying structure with diffusion, then learn to reverse the noising process.
why_it_matters: Planted diffusion; with DDPM (Ho et al. 2020, arXiv 2006.11239) became the dominant generative paradigm — and by 2025 a serious language-modeling paradigm (diffusion LLMs, domain 05).

title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
core_idea: Route each token to a few expert FFNs — parameters grow without proportional compute.
why_it_matters: Decoupling parameters from FLOPs; the backbone of frontier open models (Mixtral, DeepSeek-V3, domain 03).
